appropriate: the flat-floored arch O fits a calm Sage wordmark, but 'nothing gets dropped' only arrives if someone explains the flat floor as a ledge that holds
distinctive: the arch O is the one owned move and no hook, arrow, hexagon or node appears, yet the rest of the word is a plain geometric lowercase sans close to the category's neutral type
simple: one shape, a round-topped arch on a flat base, that anyone could draw from memory in a second
legible: 'Orvane' reads at once from 256 down to the 64 one-colour lockup; the arch stays a solid shape with an open counter at 24 and 16 px, though the counter is getting small at 16
adaptable: it holds in black, reversed, in the one-colour 64 and 32 panels, as an ochre app tile, a browser tab and a GitHub avatar; no motion logic is shown
timeless: no 'avoid' shape; the mono-initial from the wordmark is a 'use carefully' item that the strategy justifies as a symbol drawn from the name's own letters
universal: the mirrored panel reads clean because the arch is symmetric, but the rotated panel turns the O into a D, and the lone arch can faintly read as a tombstone or a doorway
clear: unsearched: arch- and doorway-shaped O monograms show up often in property, architecture and storage brands; none of Svix, Hookdeck, Convoy, Hook0 or Webhook Relay uses one that I know of
congruent: warm ochre instead of purple or blue, a flat bottom, symmetry, rounded corners and lowercase all match the targets; the wordmark's stroke is lighter than the mid-to-heavy weight asked for
system: horizontal lockups and the symbol tiers from 64 to 16 px derive cleanly, but no stacked lockup or rationale appears on the sheet
